## EMST role: Environmental compliance inspector (state variant, entry level; P1)

*Match:* `skos:broadMatch`, confidence 0.55, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R12-environmental-compliance-inspector/state:2651`). *Authority position (editorial):* regulator.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Conduct regulatory compliance inspections — entry L1 *(distinguishing)*
- Work safely on hazardous, industrial and energized field sites — entry L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — entry L1
- Manage field sample custody and field quality control — entry L1
- Maintain independence and manage conflicts of interest across the regulator-regulated boundary — entry L1
- Build and maintain a defensible administrative record — entry L1
- Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings — entry L1
- Communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty — entry L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — entry L1
- Record field observations with protocol fidelity and data integrity — entry L1
- Provide compliance and technical assistance to regulated entities and local governments — entry L1
- Assure the quality of environmental data from collection to release — entry L1
- Maintain the integrity of regulatory and scientific findings under institutional pressure — entry L1

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Inspect a permitted facility or site against its permit conditions and applicable rules, recording observations, measurements and samples as evidence — 21.9% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Write an inspection report stating findings of fact for each condition inspected, separating the inspector's observations from conclusions — 16.9% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Plan a compliance inspection from the facility's permit, compliance history and monitoring reports, listing the conditions to verify and the evidence to collect — 11.2% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Collect samples and photographs during an inspection under chain-of-custody procedures, so that the evidence is admissible in an enforcement proceeding — 11.2% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Collect grab water samples at locations and depths that represent the condition of interest, recording flow and site conditions at collection — 5.6% *(needed at entry)*
- Complete chain-of-custody records for every sample from collection to laboratory receipt, recording each transfer, seal and temperature check — 5.6% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Verify a facility's self-reported emissions or discharge values against independent remote-sensing or ambient data, stating the discrepancy and its uncertainty — 5.6% *(critical)*
- Collect field duplicates, splits and blanks at the frequency the sampling plan specifies, labelling them so the laboratory cannot identify them — 2.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Audit an environmental dataset on a set schedule, identifying errors and anomalies and recording each correction with its basis. — 2.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Answer compliance questions from regulated entities through a help line or portal, recording each question and the guidance given for consistency review — 2.8%
- Verify an AI-generated field product, such as a condition map or drafted inspection note, against observations made at the site before it is relied on — 2.8%
- Index documents into the administrative record with dates, authors and provenance labels, marking which content was produced with AI assistance — 2.8% *(needed at entry)*

*Credential gates (draft):* State environmental inspector credential (programme-issued delegation to inspect) (required); EPA Method 9 visible emissions observer certification (preferred)
